summary: Flame Atlas is a data-driven dashboard developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge “Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data.” The project aims to support fire-safety research for future lunar habitats by organizing and analyzing NASA's scattered microgravity combustion experiment records. Using NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) datasets from FLEX, BASS and SAME, we developed Python-based parsers to extract and structure experimental conditions into 333 records, presented through an interactive web dashboard. Users can filter experiments based on lunar cabin compatibility, fuel, suppressant and airflow, explore experimental conditions through bubble visualizations, and export selected records as CSV files. A key finding was that only 8 of the 290 planned FLEX tests fall within the specified lunar cabin envelope of at least 30% oxygen and a maximum pressure of 10.2 psi. The platform also highlights missing experimental parameters, inconsistencies between sources and verification statuses, ensuring that planned experiments are not misrepresented as completed tests. Overall, Flame Atlas transforms fragmented space-combustion research into accessible, structured evidence to help researchers evaluate fire-safety requirements for future lunar habitats.
